description: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (552B MoE with a 196B Engram table) on 4xH200 with SGLang TP4+EP4, DSPARK speculative decoding, an auto fp8_e4m3 KV cache and HiCache L2 at --hicache-ratio 3. notes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (2026-10-17 refresh of V4.1-Flash, same 552B MoE + 196B Engram architecture) on 4xH200. TP4+EP4, DSPARK speculative decoding, engram table on the host (SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1). --ep-size 4 is a BOOT REQUIREMENT, not a perf knob: TP-only shards experts to 576 and Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod asserts hidden/intermediate %128; EP4 keeps experts whole (96/rank). NO backend override flags -- --attention-backend and --moe-runner-backend auto-resolve to dsv4 / flashinfer_mxfp4 and overriding them is the most common cause of a disappointing measurement. MEM-FRACTION 0.775 (2026-10-30): this is the value the live pod actually runs, measured 2026-10-28. Three values had been in circulation -- 0.70 (this seed), 0.775 (live), 0.80 (docs and the memory-ledger arithmetic) -- so a redeploy from seed silently changed a memory-governing value. 0.775 is now the recorded operating point and was confirmed good. The 0.70 rung remains the COLD-CACHE SAFE baseline: deepgemm/autotune caches start cold on a fresh PVC and the 0.74/0.775 rungs only boot once those caches are warm, so fall back to 0.70 on a virgin PVC. Do not raise it to buy pool while pool utilisation is in the teens -- more pool buys nothing and ready-state headroom is the scarce good. SAMPLING 2026-10-30: --preferred-sampling-params {"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95}. The flag was MISSING from this entry even though the live pod passes it, and the value the pod passed (top_p 1.0) never took effect -- --sampling-defaults defaults to model, so the checkpoint's generation_config.json wins and the engine applies 0.95. Rather than fight that, we adopt 0.95: it is the published EVALUATION setting and the value the engine already uses. Behavioural change: NONE. Documentation change: the deployment's stated intent now matches the applied value, and /get_model_info advertises it. If a future deployment genuinely wants 1.0, set --sampling-defaults openai (the field exists with choices openai|model) and verify the applied value in the engine's finished-request line -- do not just change the flag and assume. KV CACHE DTYPE: --kv-cache-dtype is deliberately ABSENT, i.e. auto. Two of our own documents disagree about what auto resolves to (an audit recorded bf16 by auto-default; the memory ledger's 2,123 B/token arithmetic assumes fp8_e4m3), and the resolution was not readable in the v0.5.23 tree within budget. RESOLVED 2026-10-31: the engine sets fp8_e4m3. Boot line on the v0.5.23 redeploy: 'Setting KV cache dtype to fp8_e4m3 for DeepseekV4ForCausalLM' with --kv-cache-dtype absent (auto). The audit's 'bf16 by auto-default' was wrong; the memory ledger's 2,123 B/token stands; the earlier 'expect bfloat16, fp8 unavailable on SM90' inference was also wrong. SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESS_STATE_DTYPE=bf16 is NOT the KV dtype -- it sets the compressed-MLA c4/c128 STATE dtype only (accepted: float32/fp32/bfloat16/bf16), independent of --kv-cache-dtype. L3/HiCache: --hicache-ratio 3 is ON (restored to this entry 2026-10-31 -- see HICACHE RESTORED below); this model has no mamba/KDA layers and its pool is rank-replicated, so the rankless-key collision that disables L3 on GLM cannot form here. 1M context is configured but NOT yet verified end-to-end on this deployment -- run a semantic needle probe before quoting a served-context number, and note output is not bitwise stable across batch composition on this backend. Boot guard: a negative mem usage= line VOIDS the datapoint -- drain the GPUs and re-boot before citing anything from that boot. HICACHE RESTORED 2026-10-31: the redeploy that took v0.5.23 shipped from this entry WITHOUT --enable-hierarchical-cache / --hicache-ratio, silently dropping the L2 host pool the previous pod ran. This entry never carried the flags (seed<->pod drift -- the audit recorded the pod, the seed recorded less), so they are restored here verbatim: --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 3 --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-write-policy write_through. POD MEMORY RESTORED WITH THEM: at ratio 3 the host pool is ~3 x ~31 GiB/rank device pool at 0.775 ~= 372 GiB node-wide, plus ~97 GiB shared engram host table (measured 2026-10-30: 'engram host table layer 1: layout=shared, 96681 MiB resident, 100% huge pages') plus ~30 GiB runtime ~= 500 GiB. The previous request 350Gi / limit 512Gi would have clamped the pool at boot via the guard min(psutil.available, cgroup_headroom) - 10 GiB -- the pod would have booted 'fine' with a silently smaller host tier. Restored to the measured pair: request 800Gi / limit 950Gi (previous pod: 598Gi working set under 950Gi). READ THE BOOT LINE 'Allocating ... hierarchical ... host pool': if the cgroup clamped it, the pool is smaller than ratio 3 implies and the LIMIT is the thing to raise. NOTE prefill CUDA graphs need no headroom here: upstream auto-disables them for DeepSeek-V4 ('Breakable CUDA graph is incompatible with DeepSeek-V4'). What stays is the prefill/decode visibility that matters: the compact 'Prefill batch' / 'Decode batch' lines (new-token, cached-token, token usage, input throughput, est. prefill TFLOPS/s -- verified in the live pod's log at 2026-11-02T15:32Z) plus --enable-request-time-stats-logging (ReqTimeStats queue_duration / forward_duration per request). The workaround existed only because v0.5.22 turned breakable prefill graphs on (#42845) and they crashed in _kda_track_ssm_kernel -- the mode-1 branch loads the bf16 SSM pool while the else branch loads the fp32 chunk-boundary snapshot, and Triton rejects the type mismatch across the runtime if. PR #44886 (kda: Align graph tracking branch dtype with the recurrent state pool) merged 2026-10-21, and the v0.5.23 tree's kernels/ops/mamba/kda_prefill_track.py is byte-identical to that PR head (blob ce3b49ea), so the fix is in the release. #43657 is a stale duplicate against the pre-move filename (kernels/ops/attention/fla/kda_prefill_graph_track.py, which 404s at v0.5.23) and its regression test never merged -- so re-enable behind a smoke test, not blind. EXPLICIT breakable RATHER THAN DELETING THE FLAG: they are identical today (arg_groups/fields/exec_.py declares cuda_graph_backend_prefill as Optional[Literal[full,breakable,disabled]] default None; model_executor/cuda_graph_config.py default_prefill_backend() returns BREAKABLE on CUDA for every model, not model-conditionally), but this deployment has already been bitten once by a default that moved under it (#42845), so the operating point is pinned explicitly at zero behavioural cost. REMOVED 2026-10-30: --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.9 (inert -- --max-mamba-cache-size 480 pins the KDA pool absolutely, so the ratio sizes nothing; the live pod never passed it, and seed<->pod parity was the finding) and the --log-requests block (--log-requests + --log-requests-level 0). --enable-cache-report STAYS: it is what populates usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, and its absence is silent. RESOURCES: limit_memory 800Gi -> 830Gi (2026-10-30) -> 835Gi (2026-10-30 evening redeploy). The pod sat at 737 GiB / 800 GiB = 92%, which trips MlisPredictorMemoryCritical (>90 for 5m); 737/835 = 88.3% clears that rule. NOT CLEARED BY THIS: the generic Container-has-a-high-memory-usage alert fires at 80% and would need ~921 GiB to silence. The HiCache host pool is ratio-implied (--hicache-ratio 6.0 -> 127.61 GB/rank, measured in the v5 boot log) and was NOT clamped by the old limit, so raising the limit adds headroom without growing the pool -- confirm the boot line Allocating hierarchical KV cache host pool is unchanged after redeploy. L3 storage tier stays OFF: the file evictor makes rank 0 the sole storage owner on MLA models while this model's KDA/mamba state is TP-sharded and routed to every rank, and the storage keys carry no rank -- an L3 restore then feeds rank 0's shard to every rank (re-checked against the v3 tree at ba94488b on 2026-10-06; unchanged). WATCH: the chat template defaults to reasoning_effort=max with clear_thinking=false, i.e. full reasoning budget and prior-turn reasoning retained (2026-10-22 decision -- the model default is more believable than a hand-tuned flag). If repeated-block loops appear on long multi-turn agentic traffic, the untried compromise is clear_thinking:true with effort left at max: full reasoning budget, history stripped. name: deepseek-v41-flash-1017-mooncake
description: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (552B MoE with a 196B Engram table) on 4xH200 with SGLang TP4+EP4, DSPARK speculative decoding, an auto fp8_e4m3 KV cache and HiCache L2 at --hicache-ratio 3. EP4 is a boot requirement, not a perf knob: TP-only sharding trips the MoE method's %128 assertion. Boot at mem-fraction 0.8 (live ISVC). HiCache L3 on the shared Mooncake store.
notes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (2026-10-17 refresh of V4.1-Flash, same 552B MoE + 196B Engram architecture) on 4xH200. TP4+EP4, DSPARK speculative decoding, engram table on the host (SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1). --ep-size 4 is a BOOT REQUIREMENT, not a perf knob: TP-only shards experts to 576 and Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod asserts hidden/intermediate %128; EP4 keeps experts whole (96/rank). NO backend override flags -- --attention-backend and --moe-runner-backend auto-resolve to dsv4 / flashinfer_mxfp4 and overriding them is the most common cause of a disappointing measurement. MEM-FRACTION 0.775 (2026-10-30): this is the value the live pod actually runs, measured 2026-10-28. Three values had been in circulation -- 0.70 (this seed), 0.775 (live), 0.80 (docs and the memory-ledger arithmetic) -- so a redeploy from seed silently changed a memory-governing value. 0.775 is now the recorded operating point and was confirmed good. The 0.70 rung remains the COLD-CACHE SAFE baseline: deepgemm/autotune caches start cold on a fresh PVC and the 0.74/0.775 rungs only boot once those caches are warm, so fall back to 0.70 on a virgin PVC. Do not raise it to buy pool while pool utilisation is in the teens -- more pool buys nothing and ready-state headroom is the scarce good. SAMPLING 2026-10-30: --preferred-sampling-params {"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95}. The flag was MISSING from this entry even though the live pod passes it, and the value the pod passed (top_p 1.0) never took effect -- --sampling-defaults defaults to model, so the checkpoint's generation_config.json wins and the engine applies 0.95. Rather than fight that, we adopt 0.95: it is the published EVALUATION setting and the value the engine already uses. Behavioural change: NONE. Documentation change: the deployment's stated intent now matches the applied value, and /get_model_info advertises it. If a future deployment genuinely wants 1.0, set --sampling-defaults openai (the field exists with choices openai|model) and verify the applied value in the engine's finished-request line -- do not just change the flag and assume. KV CACHE DTYPE: --kv-cache-dtype is deliberately ABSENT, i.e. auto. Two of our own documents disagree about what auto resolves to (an audit recorded bf16 by auto-default; the memory ledger's 2,123 B/token arithmetic assumes fp8_e4m3), and the resolution was not readable in the v0.5.23 tree within budget. RESOLVED 2026-10-31: the engine sets fp8_e4m3. Boot line on the v0.5.23 redeploy: 'Setting KV cache dtype to fp8_e4m3 for DeepseekV4ForCausalLM' with --kv-cache-dtype absent (auto). The audit's 'bf16 by auto-default' was wrong; the memory ledger's 2,123 B/token stands; the earlier 'expect bfloat16, fp8 unavailable on SM90' inference was also wrong. SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESS_STATE_DTYPE=bf16 is NOT the KV dtype -- it sets the compressed-MLA c4/c128 STATE dtype only (accepted: float32/fp32/bfloat16/bf16), independent of --kv-cache-dtype. L3/HiCache: --hicache-ratio 3 is ON (restored to this entry 2026-10-31 -- see HICACHE RESTORED below); this model has no mamba/KDA layers and its pool is rank-replicated, so the rankless-key collision that disables L3 on GLM cannot form here. 1M context is configured but NOT yet verified end-to-end on this deployment -- run a semantic needle probe before quoting a served-context number, and note output is not bitwise stable across batch composition on this backend. Boot guard: a negative mem usage= line VOIDS the datapoint -- drain the GPUs and re-boot before citing anything from that boot. MAMBA RATIO .6 -- cookbook formula r = (S + D) x token_equiv / L, token_equiv = state_bytes / kv_bytes_per_token = 2394 for bf16 state over fp8 KV. S = state slots per running request: extra_buffer=5, extra_buffer_lazy=4 (this entry), no_buffer=3, disabled radix cache=1. D = 8. So r = 28,728 / L at S=4. MEASURED balance point: 88 device state slots / 4 = 22 concurrent, and 841,856 KV tokens / 22 = ~38K tokens per request -- i.e. 0.6 balances at a ~38K average request length on this card. If real traffic averages ~16K the ratio should rise (~1.5 gives ~36 concurrent); if it averages ~38K this is already balanced. Re-derive rather than guessing; the balanced ratio is VRAM-independent. MEASURED DEVICE LEDGER at 0.825: weights 20.14 + draft 3.72 GB; mamba cache 19.65 GB (conv 0.24 + ssm 6.26 + intermediate_ssm 12.94 + intermediate_conv 0.21) = 88 slots = 4 per request; KV target 841,856 tokens = 27.59 GB; KV draft 8.02 GB; available_gpu_mem 12.75 GB at startup, 13.4 GB after draft verify graphs. EFFECTIVE STATE COST IS 223 MB/SLOT, not the 78.4 MB raw state: --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy materialises ~13.15 GB of intermediate buffers, roughly 3x the per-slot cost. Budget the state pool on 223 MB/slot, not 78.4. CONTEXT AND CAPACITY: context_len=262144 (MEASURED at startup) -- the full 262K window is served, not a reduced one. But the device KV pool is 841,856 tokens = 3.21x the context, so only ~3 requests fit at FULL context; a single 262K request consumes a third of the entire device pool. The 22-concurrent figure is a ~38K-average figure, not a 262K one. The HiCache host KV tier (2,525,632 tokens) holds ~9.6 full-context sequences. Size expectations against the real request-length distribution, not against 262K. max_running_requests: asking for 64 got 22. The engine logs 'max_running_requests is capped to 22 by the mamba state cache (max_mamba_cache_size=88, 4 state slots per request)'. The cap is the state pool, not a misconfiguration. HIERARCHICAL CACHES -- THERE ARE THREE DISTINCT HOST POOLS, not one, and a pod budget must sum them. All MEASURED at ratio 3 on 2026-11-17, each allocated within ~60 s of the others, KV FIRST: (1) target KV host pool: 2,525,632 tokens = 82.76 GB -- exactly 3x the 27.59 GB device KV pool, 32 KiB/token; (2) hierarchical MAMBA cache: 20.79 GB = 265 state slots at 78.5 MB/slot = 3.01x the 88 device slots, layout=page_first -- it stores the RAW state only, so the device's 13.15 GB of intermediate buffers are NOT mirrored; (3) draft KV host pool: 2,525,632 tokens = 25.86 GB -- 3x the draft's 8.02 GB device pool, 10 KiB/token. Do NOT size the pod off the first 'Allocating kv hierarchical KV host pool' line alone -- that is 82.76 GB of a 129.41 GB total, and sizing to it is the mistake this entry made once. Note also that the three pools total 129 GB rather than 3x the whole device footprint (166 GB) precisely because the mamba intermediates are not mirrored. Expect that in TTFT-post. Radix cache is impl=UnifiedRadixCache with components FULL + MAMBA (hybrid_ssm=True, hicache_attached=True). To make it serve, bake vLLM 0.32.0 + nemo-speech into an image (the vllmaudio family is the natural home) and repoint image; engine.validated is empty because that pair was never booted. The other route is the Nemotron Transcribe NIM, which the card says is about 2x faster because its kernels are not upstream yet -- but the card publishes no container coordinates for it (the NGC link is a model, not an image), so it is not encodable here. QUANT: FP8 is NVIDIA's ModelOpt PTQ of nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B. Every benchmark number in the card is the BF16 checkpoint's; averaged over the transcription benchmarks FP8's error rate is 1.0% higher in RELATIVE terms. NO eval BLOCK ON PURPOSE: tests/test_eval_field.py asserts seed entries carry none, so the catalog badges this row 'unvalidated' -- which is the truth, nothing here was booted. ARGS are the card's single-GPU profile verbatim, plus --download-dir/--host/--port for a PCAI row. The non-obvious ones: --dtype bfloat16 is the compute/residual dtype and does NOT dequantize the weights, the FP8 checkpoint stays FP8. --kv-cache-dtype auto must STAY auto -- config.json declares the checkpoint's own FP8 KV scheme (fp8_e4m3) and vLLM derives the scale layout from it; forcing fp8 re-derives scales. --no-enable-prefix-caching is mandatory alongside ReplaySSM. --use-replayssm + --mamba-backend flashinfer + --mamba-cache-mode none are one triple: ReplaySSM replays the SSM state instead of recomputing it, and that is exactly what makes prefix caching impossible. --speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8} is MTP8, the deeper of the two depths the model was trained for; drop the flag to disable spec decoding. --limit-mm-per-prompt audio length 57600000 is samples at 16 kHz = one hour and count 1 is one recording per request, because the model transcribes offline -- its internal chunking does NOT make it streaming. --trust-request-mm-kwargs plus --middleware nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm.ctc_serving.ctc_timestamp_middleware are what turn on CTC word timestamps and speaker diarization, and word timestamps REQUIRE the V1 model runner, hence VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0. --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 exposes the reasoning block; reasoning is toggled per request via chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking, and the card's sampling profile is task-dependent: temperature 0 with reasoning off for transcription/translation/LID, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 with reasoning on for audio understanding. --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 is the card's value for the 96 GB cell. STARTUP: the log must show quantization=modelopt and 128 FP8 audio-encoder linear layers before the boot is trustworthy. FIRST BOOT IS SLOW -- FlashInfer compiles kernels on first use and needs nvcc, and the card warns startup takes several minutes, so size the MLIS readiness probe for that or the pod is killed mid-compile. The compile cache lives under $FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE/.cache/flashinfer and XDG_CACHE_HOME does NOT move it; the catalog has no volume field, so if /mnt/models is writable in the serving pod set FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE to a per-(runtime,arch) PVC path such as /mnt/models/.flashinfer/vllm-0.32.0-sm120 and stop every restart repaying the compile.
